Question: Have you ever overcome your stock market loss? How?
Old_Answer: Have you ever overcome your stock market loss? How?: For a trader losses are like frequent unwanted guests. You are forced to meet and greet them and by the time they leave there is a hole in your pocket. There is no avoiding them but they need to be managed. There visits are to be kept to a minimum and expenses on them should be on a tight budget. Yes, I am talking about keeping the losses to a minimum. Easier said than done. Stock market losses are like guests overstaying and causing more financial stress. Well, like every other trader I too have seen some big losses. On most occasions, I have come through the situation reasonably well and back to profit making very soon. The first such instance occurred in January 2015 : The loss in the month was Rs. 127718. I had tried selling options this month because it is the conventional wisdom of the market. Little good it did to me. I was left licking my wounds. An introspection was required and done. One should do what one is good at. I was good at making money through buying options. I had gone for something which was not my strength. So decided to stick to option buying. This was the outcome in February 2015: Things worked out well and the loss from previous month was wiped out. Kept my faith in my trading methods and did more of the same over next month as well. Result for March 2015: There was a profit of Rs. 270242 at the end of the month for my humble efforts. Lessons Learnt : These are old trades but important to me for the following reasons: (1) I learnt that losses can be overcome by staying patient with your method. You just have to keep the belief. (2) Leave the profits to the market. Do not get out from a good trade in a hurry. (3) Trade as per your strength not what the others tell you to do. What Happened Next ? : With all the lessons learnt, I am still a human being. Humans make errors. I too made many of them and in November 2015 ( just 8 months later) was looking at a loss of Rs. 145000. December 2015 too ended in a loss of Rs. 10000. It took two more months with profits of Rs. 65000 and Rs. 166000 respectively in January and February 2016. Once again the losses could be erased and profitability restored. The year 2018 Loss : I share my stock selection and trades on OptionsNext. From May 2018, I posted about option buying trades. The first 3 months ended profitable. In August there was the visit by the unwanted guest— the big loss. Whether it was PUT buying or CALL buying, it was a losing proposition. The loss was Rs. 99589. In January 2015 I was a lonely trader like most traders are. it did not matter what I lost as no one else was involved. In August 2018, there were people reading my posts and some even taking the trades. They too lost money along with me. Every loss in the market is loss of credibility in the minds of the people with whom you are sharing the trades. You start doubting your methods. It was difficult but necessary to keep the belief. September 2018 : I kept doing what was normal. The crisis in ILFS and the crash in the markets on September 21, 2018 helped in a big way. The results were wonderful. A profit of Rs. 430609. The memories of the previous month were wiped away with the fortune smiling on my trades in September 2018. Subsequently October and November months too have been alright though nowhere near the heady high of September. Summary : I have shared my recovery from losses. The HOW part of the question is more important. The recovery was possible due to: Keeping the belief in my selection process and trading method. Trusting the market to give me the profit in the right trades. Knowing my losses in the wrong trades. Doing what I am supposedly good at i.e buying options even though the conventional wisdom is against it. The losses do create self doubts but if you are able to recover from the losses on multiple occasions by following the same set of rules that leads to self belief which is a trader’s most powerful asset. The discovery of this process in 2015 through the big loss experiences has been very good for me. I trust that the readers too will benefit from these experiences. It is always better to learn from the losses of others. Thanks for reading.

Answer_with_writing_sample: What does it mean to say that the stock market is a bubble? A bubble in the stock market refers to a situation where the prices of stocks rise significantly above their intrinsic value, driven by exuberant market behavior rather than fundamental economic indicators. This phenomenon often occurs when investors become overly optimistic, leading to speculative buying, which inflates prices even further. The classic signs of a bubble include rapid price increases, widespread media coverage, and a general belief that prices will continue to rise indefinitely. However, as history has shown, bubbles eventually burst, resulting in a sharp decline in stock prices, often leading to significant financial losses for investors. The dot-com bubble of the late 1990s and the housing bubble of the mid-2000s are prime examples where irrational exuberance led to unsustainable price levels, followed by dramatic corrections. It’s essential to understand that while bubbles can create opportunities for short-term gains, they also carry substantial risks. Investors should remain vigilant and grounded in fundamental analysis, rather than getting swept away by market euphoria. In essence, recognizing a bubble requires a keen awareness of market dynamics and a disciplined approach to investing, as the aftermath of a bubble can be painful for those who fail to heed the warning signs. Thanks for reading.

Historically, we have seen notable examples of bubbles, such as the dot-com bubble in the late 1990s and the housing bubble leading up to the 2008 financial crisis. Understanding the dynamics of bubbles is crucial for investors, as it highlights the importance of grounding investment decisions in fundamental analysis rather than succumbing to the allure of market euphoria.
